label: Carbon, in vivo and hyperpolarized
reference: Tetramethylsilane at 0 ppm. Every in vivo 13C resonance lies downfield of TMS, so every value in this table is positive and larger ppm is further left; in practice the scale is set from a known line rather than an added standard, the lipid methylene at 30.2 ppm for natural abundance work or the injected pyruvate C1 at 171.0 ppm in a hyperpolarized study.
note: Heights are schematic and span two different experiments on one axis: the hyperpolarized [1-13C]pyruvate lines at 183.2, 179.4, 176.5, 171.0 and 161.0 ppm exist only for about a minute after injection and sit five orders of magnitude above thermal equilibrium, while everything else is a natural abundance or 13C-enriched steady-state signal acquired with 1H decoupling, without which every line here splits into a 125 to 170 Hz multiplet that shrinks in ppm as the field rises.

peaks.name: Lac C1
peaks.note: In a hyperpolarized [1-13C]pyruvate study this is the label transfer product and the peak that carries kPL: 12.2 ppm downfield of pyruvate, about 392 Hz at 3T and 915 Hz at 7T. It is also the carboxyl of the endogenous lactate pool at natural abundance. Reported 183.0 to 183.3 ppm.

peaks.name: Glu C5
peaks.note: Anchor for the amino acid carbonyl region, roughly 174 to 184 ppm, which also holds NAA C1 179.8, Gln C5 178.6, Asp C4 178.4, Glu C1 175.4, Asp C1 175.0, Gln C1 174.9 and NAA C5 174.3. Carbonyls have no directly bonded proton, so they gain little NOE and relax slowly by chemical shift anisotropy, and are under-represented unless TR is long.

peaks.name: Pyr hydr
peaks.note: Not a metabolic product. It is the hydration equilibrium of the pyruvate ketone carried in with the injectate, 8.4 ppm and about 270 Hz at 3T downfield of pyruvate. Useful as a marker that the pyruvate line is where you think it is. Reported 179.4 to 179.5 ppm.

peaks.name: Ala C1
peaks.note: Made from pyruvate by alanine aminotransferase; prominent in liver and skeletal muscle, weak in brain and prostate. 5.5 ppm and about 177 Hz at 3T downfield of pyruvate. Reported between 176.5 and 177.1 ppm depending on the spectral model.

peaks.name: Lip C=O
peaks.note: Centre of a 172.3 to 173.3 ppm cluster that splits by sn position on the glycerol backbone. No attached proton, so small NOE and a long T1; it is systematically underestimated in a short-TR natural abundance acquisition.

peaks.name: Pyr C1
peaks.full: Pyruvate C1 (carboxyl), the injected hyperpolarized label
peaks.note: Dominates the spectrum for the first 30 s or so after a 0.43 mL/kg bolus of 250 mM [1-13C]pyruvate, then decays with an in vivo T1 near 20 to 45 s at 3T. Reported 170.5 to 171.1 ppm; it is the working frequency reference for the whole hyperpolarized set.

peaks.name: HCO3-
peaks.note: The only in vivo readout of pyruvate dehydrogenase flux, 10.0 ppm and about 321 Hz at 3T upfield of pyruvate. Small, since kPB runs about a sixth of kPL, and the first peak lost to spectral leakage from lactate. Its exchange partner 13CO2 sits near 125 ppm but is roughly 20-fold smaller at pH 7.4 (pKa 6.1) and is not usually resolved in humans.

peaks.name: Lip C=C
peaks.note: Centre of a 127 to 132 ppm envelope whose sub-peaks separate monounsaturated from polyunsaturated positions. This resolution, which 1H cannot provide, is the main reason to do hepatic or adipose lipid composition by 13C. 1J(CH) about 155 to 160 Hz.

peaks.name: Glyc C1
peaks.note: Essentially 100 percent NMR visible in vivo (in vivo to enzymatic ratio 0.95 +/- 0.05). Liver 200 to 300 mM and skeletal muscle 60 to 100 mM glucosyl units are both detectable at natural abundance; brain glycogen at 3 to 5 mM is not, and needs labelled glucose infusion. 1J(CH) about 170 Hz.

peaks.name: bGlc C1
peaks.note: The more abundant anomer, about 64 percent at equilibrium, hence taller than the alpha line. Reported 96.7 to 96.8 ppm, well clear of glycogen C1 at 100.5.

peaks.name: aGlc C1
peaks.note: About 36 percent of the anomeric equilibrium. With the beta line it gives the cleanest window on tissue glucose during a [1-13C]glucose infusion; the other glucose carbons pile up between 61 and 77 ppm and are not separately useful in vivo.

peaks.name: Glu C2
peaks.note: Only 0.6 ppm from Gln C2, which is 19 Hz at 3T and 45 Hz at 7T, so the C2 pair is realistically usable only at 4T and above. NAA C2 at 54.0 and Asp C2 at 53.2 crowd the same region.

peaks.name: Gln C2
peaks.note: Reported 54.9 to 55.1 ppm. Sits on the upfield shoulder of Glu C2 and is fitted rather than resolved below 4T.

peaks.name: Asp C3
peaks.note: The aspartate line normally quantified; Asp C2 at 53.2 ppm falls inside the crowded alpha carbon region. Label reaches it from oxaloacetate, so its turnover reports the TCA intermediate pool and anaplerosis rather than the glutamate pools.

peaks.name: Glu C4
peaks.note: The primary readout of [1-13C]glucose and [2-13C]acetate infusion; its turnover curve gives the TCA cycle flux. Labelled on the first turn of the cycle, so it rises fastest of the glutamate carbons. Quoted between 34.2 and 34.4 ppm.

peaks.name: Gln C4
peaks.note: 2.5 ppm upfield of Glu C4, which is 80 Hz at 3T and 188 Hz at 7T. Separating this pair is the whole reason to measure glutamate to glutamine cycling with 13C instead of 1H. Quoted between 31.7 and 31.9 ppm.

peaks.name: Lip CH2
peaks.note: The tallest line in any natural abundance 13C spectrum taken with a surface coil, quoted between 29.9 and 30.5 ppm, and the usual internal frequency reference. Other acyl chain carbons nearby: alpha to carbonyl 34.1, allylic 27.2, diallylic 25.6, beta 25.0, omega-2 22.7.

peaks.name: Glu C3
peaks.note: Labelled on the second turn of the TCA cycle, so it lags C4; that lag is what constrains the exchange rate between the TCA intermediates and the amino acid pools in the metabolic model. Quoted 27.8 to 27.9 ppm.

peaks.name: Gln C3
peaks.note: Only 0.8 ppm from Glu C3, 26 Hz at 3T, and it sits under the allylic lipid carbons near 27.2 ppm as well. The least reliable of the six Glu and Gln resonances. Quoted 27.1 to 27.2 ppm.

peaks.name: NAA C6
peaks.note: A sharp line with a large NOE and the most prominent metabolite peak in a natural abundance brain 13C spectrum. The other NAA carbons are C2 54.0, C3 40.3, C5 174.3 and C1 179.8. Quoted 22.8 to 23.0 ppm.

peaks.name: Lac C3
peaks.note: The natural abundance and infusion readout of the lactate pool; the same molecule's C1 is at 183.2 ppm. Quoted 20.8 to 21.0 ppm, close enough to the omega-2 lipid carbon at 22.7 that it can be buried in muscle or in any voxel with subcutaneous fat contamination.

peaks.name: Lip CH3
peaks.note: The upfield end of the in vivo 13C spectrum. One methyl per acyl chain, so its ratio to the 30.2 ppm methylene envelope gives the mean chain length.
